properties.name: Mount Eden / Johnson Landing salt works (SR-92 to Hayward Landing)
properties.note: John Johnson leveed 14 acres of naturally saline marsh at Mt Eden in 1853 (first harvest 25 t, shipped by schooner), just north of today's SR-92 - the first solar salt works on the Bay (EDAW 2005 after Sandoval 1988); the natural salinas here are on the 1857 Coast Survey T-sheet (SFEI) and USFWS's 'natural salt ponds c.1850'. Small family works (American Salt Co., Marsicano family, from the early 1860s) followed. Ponds and crystallizers still drawn at Johnson Landing on the 1942 Hayward sheet (1939 photos). Works on ground that is marsh or fill today end c.1955 (LOW).

properties.name: Hayward shore salt works (Hayward Landing to San Lorenzo Creek)
properties.note: Ver Planck's (1958) map of the old works places Chris Madsen, H. and P.J. Mathiesen, Tuckson, C. and D. Pestdorf and the Haywards Landing crude plant on this shore; the USC&GS 1907 chart draws pond levees from Russell (Hayward) Landing south. Absorbed by California Salt Co. (1901) and Leslie-California (1924); by the 1939 photos (1942 Hayward sheet) only ditches and dry diked land are left. Start ESTIMATED from USFWS's c.1870 eras panel; end ESTIMATED c.1930.

properties.name: Mount Eden salt works between SR-92 and Mt Eden Creek (Nielsen, Michelson, Peterman, Whisby, Oliver, Ohlsen)
properties.note: Lopez (1971) works A-G (EDAW 2005 fig. 13): M. Nielsen's Rock Springs, J. Michelson's Rocky Point (pre-1898), Peterman's Mt Eden Salt Works, Whisby, Ohlsen - all merged into Oliver Salt by 1909 - and Andrew Oliver's own 120 acres bought 1872 (Ver Planck 1958:110). Ponds here on USFWS's c.1870 eras panel. Start ESTIMATED 1860s.

properties.name: Union Pacific Salt Co. works (Mt Eden Creek to Old Alameda Creek)
properties.note: Union Pacific Salt Co., in continuous production 1872-1927 (Sandoval 1988); in 1882 it occupied 1,200 acres of marsh near the mouths of Alameda Creek and Mount Eden (Union City) Slough, five concentrating ponds of 100-300 acres and many 6-8 acre crystallizers, some floored with boards (Ver Planck 1958:108). Lopez (1971) works H (and M, Sinclair's Occidental, east).

properties.name: Barton's Solar (Pioneer) and Carmen Island salt works (bay side, Old Alameda Creek to Coyote Hill Slough)
properties.note: Lopez (1971) works I (B.F. Barton's Solar Salt Works, in operation by 1885, later Pioneer Salt, bought by Oliver 1927) and J (Carmen Island, one of the four producers over 10,000 t a year in 1900; California Salt Co. 1901). Ponds to the bay edge on the USC&GS 1907 chart and the USGS 1896 survey ('SALT WORKS'). Start ESTIMATED c.1880.

properties.name: Alvarado, Union City and Turk Island salt works (landward, Old Alameda Creek to Coyote Hill Slough)
properties.note: Lopez (1971) works N (John Quigley's Alvarado Salt Works near Barron's Landing, 1862, independent to 1909), O (Plummer Brothers' Turk Island works, 1869), K (Putnam's Union City Salt Works, on the 1896 USGS survey at Alvarado) and L (Continental Salt & Chemical, 1900). Start ESTIMATED mid-1860s.

properties.name: Union City Alvarado salt ponds (upland edge, levees 1924-31)
properties.note: Recorded resource P-01-010834: levees and ponds built 1924-31, flood-control levees 1955-59 (Shoup and Baker 2007); not among Lopez's 1860-1910 works. Before: the landward edge of the marsh at Alvarado.

properties.name: Diked marsh at the north end of the Coyote Hills (Patterson Ranch)
properties.note: Levees around marsh (tufts inside) on the 1942 Hayward sheet (1939 photos); natural marsh on the 1896 survey. Grazing / duck-club land of the Patterson Ranch; Coyote Hills Regional Park marsh today. Year = first map that shows the levees.

properties.name: Salt ponds south of Coyote Hill Slough (DL&IC / Whitney 1907-08)
properties.note: Still marsh on the USC&GS 1907 chart. In May 1907 DL&IC was 'reclaiming 2,000 acres' for salt 'on land adjoining California Salt Works' holdings' and Whitney planned to flood 2,000 acres north of Dumbarton Point (EDAW 2005); Lopez (1971) marks works P ('Restdorf's, merged later with Arden') here. Fully ponded on the 1942 sheet (1939 photos).

properties.name: Arden Salt Co. ponds, Coyote Hills to Dumbarton Point
properties.note: Natural marsh on the 1896 survey and the 1907 chart. Arden Salt Co. was formed by August Schilling in 1919 to make salt on the Dumbarton Land & Improvement Co. marsh around Dumbarton Point ('original site Arden Salt Co.' on Ver Planck's map at the east end of the Dumbarton Bridge); evaporators on the 1942 sheet (1939 photos).

properties.name: Crystal Salt Works (Plummer Bros.) at Plummer Landing, Newark
properties.note: 'Crystal Salt Works' at Plummer Landing on the 1896 USGS survey (Haywards 1899) - the only works south of the Coyote Hills then; Plummer Brothers, salt makers from 1869 (Ver Planck 1958). Small; the rest of the Newark marsh was untouched. Start ESTIMATED. Today the Cargill Newark plant's crystallizers.

properties.name: Arden / Leslie Newark ponds, Dumbarton Point to Mowry Slough
properties.note: Natural marsh on the 1896-99 surveys. Arden Salt (1919) worked the DL&IC marsh 'from Alviso east and north up toward Dumbarton Point' in the 1920s (EDAW 2005); Morton Salt refinery at Newark 1926, Newark No. 1 / No. 2 crude plants (Arden and Leslie). Evaporators north of Mowry Slough on the 1942-43 sheets (1939-40 photos). Year ESTIMATED mid-1920s.

properties.name: Mowry ponds M1-M3 (Mowry Slough to Coyote Creek, west)
properties.note: Marsh (tufts) inside a perimeter levee on the 1941/1943 Palo Alto sheets (1939-40 photos); salt evaporators on the 1953 Mountain View sheet (1948 photos) and Leslie's 1953 map. Leslie's ponds grew from 12,000 acres (1936) to 25,000 (1946).

properties.name: Mowry ponds M4-M6 (along Coyote Creek, west of the railroad)
properties.note: 'Salt Beds' on the 1943 San Jose sheet (1939 photos); natural marsh in 1896-99. Arden Salt in the 1920s (EDAW 2005). Year ESTIMATED mid-1920s.

properties.name: Alviso Salt Co. ponds, Charleston Slough to Guadalupe Slough (A1-A4)
properties.note: Untouched marsh on the 1899 Palo Alto sheet. Continental Salt & Chemical bought the marsh 'west of Alviso to Mayfield Slough' from Spring Valley Water Co. (contract 1921, purchase 1924); Bancroft maps of 1921 and 1929 show ponds across to Mayfield Slough; Alviso Salt Co. 1929, absorbed by Arden 1929-31 (EDAW 2005, Ver Planck 1958). Leveed but dry on the 1941/1943 sheets (1939-40 photos: idle pond beds with relict sloughs), salt evaporators again on the 1953 sheet.

properties.name: Ponds A5 / A7 (Guadalupe Slough to Alviso Slough)
properties.note: Tidal marsh on the 1941/1943 Palo Alto sheets (1939-40 photos); salt evaporators on the 1953 Mountain View sheet (1948 photos). Leslie Salt's 1940s expansion.

properties.name: Alviso Salt Co. plant ponds west of Alviso (A8)
properties.note: 'Salt Beds' with crystallizer rows on the 1943 San Jose sheet (1939 photos). Earlier attempts around Alviso in the 1890s-1910s washed away; Alviso Salt Co.'s plant near the town ran one year (1929) before Arden took it over (EDAW 2005). Year ESTIMATED late 1920s.

properties.name: Ponds A9-A11 (Alviso Slough to Coyote Creek, west of the railroad)
properties.note: Tidal marsh on the 1943 San Jose sheet (1939 photos); salt evaporators on the 1953 Mountain View / Milpitas sheets (1948 photos). DL&IC had leveed this marsh for farming in 1907-08 ('over 4,000 acres in Santa Clara County under levee, only 500 rented'); the levees were abandoned and washed out (Lopez 1971, EDAW 2005).

properties.name: Ponds A12-A18 (railroad to Artesian Slough / Coyote Creek)
properties.note: DL&IC's failed 1907-08 levees (Lopez 1971); tidal marsh on the 1943 San Jose sheet and still on the 1953 Milpitas sheet (1948 photos); salt evaporators on the 1961 Milpitas sheet. Year ESTIMATED (1953-61).

properties.name: Diked marsh east of Coyote Creek (Milpitas / North San Jose margin)
properties.note: Tidal marsh on the 1899 San Jose sheet; leveed farm ground beyond the marsh edge on the 1943 sheet (1939 photos). DL&IC had 'over 4,000 acres in Santa Clara County under levee, only 500 rented' in 1908, most abandoned after (EDAW 2005). Year ESTIMATED between the two maps.

properties.name: Island ponds A19-A21 (Coyote Creek to Mud Slough, Drawbridge)
properties.note: Marsh around Drawbridge on the 1943 and 1953 sheets (Leslie's late-1930s levees cut Drawbridge off from the bay - Mud Slough navigable only by Coast Guard / USGS boats by 1939); evaporators on the 1961 Milpitas sheet. Breached 2006 (fill_zones sb_island_ponds_restored). Year ESTIMATED (1953-61).

properties.name: Ponds A22 / A23 (north of Mud Slough, Warm Springs)
properties.note: 'Reclaimed by DL&I Co., 1907-08' (Lopez 1971) - farming levees that were abandoned; leveed dry land on the 1953 Milpitas sheet, evaporators on the 1961 sheet. Year ESTIMATED (1953-61).

properties.name: Ravenswood ponds (R1-R5, S5; Menlo Park / East Palo Alto)
properties.note: Tidal marsh with tufts on the 1943 Palo Alto sheet (1940 photos); levee-enclosed ponds on the 1948 Redwood Point sheet; 'Salt Evaporators' on the 1959-61 sheets. EDAW (2005): Leslie developed the west bay unit into evaporation ponds during the 1940s for its Redwood City plant (Leslie bought the Redwood City marshes in 1940; first salt 1951); pond S5 pumphouse built 1943-48 (aerials, SBSPRP Phase 2 EIS/R). The '1910s' in USFWS 2009 does not fit the 1940 map.

properties.name: Palo Alto baylands diked (yacht harbor, airport)
properties.note: Untouched marsh on the 1899 Palo Alto sheet; levees and dry diked ground around the Palo Alto Yacht Harbor and airport on the 1941/1943 sheets (1939-40 photos). Year ESTIMATED (yacht harbor late 1920s, airport mid-1930s; flood basin 1950s).

properties.name: San Jose / Santa Clara sewage plant ponds (Alviso)
properties.note: SFEI c.1998 'storage pond': the San Jose / Santa Clara Water Pollution Control Plant (opened 1956) oxidation and sludge ponds on former marsh / diked farm land; not salt ponds. Before: tidal marsh (1899), diked farm ground (1939 photos). Year LOW.

properties.name: Sunnyvale sewage plant oxidation ponds
properties.note: SFEI c.1998 'storage pond': Sunnyvale Water Pollution Control Plant (1956) oxidation ponds on the former Alviso Salt Co. levees / marsh; not salt ponds. Year LOW (plant opening).
